mutations.label: CONTROL (must be MISSED): a section comment reworded, which no test can see
the Content-Type gate is dropped, so a cross-origin text/plain form reaches every POST
the Content-Type gate accepts anything NON-json (inert: the paired positive)
cross-site is no longer refused (the Sec-Fetch-Site tier goes inert)
the origin/host compare is dropped, so an older browser's cross-origin POST lands
the draft's origin parse returns: '//'-rewritten then '//'-prefixed, hostname None for every real Origin
the guard marker is never set, so a new unguarded POST would pass the enumeration
one endpoint loses its guard (/delete), which is what an exception list would allow to rot
the opt-in widens to truthiness, so a settings file holding the string "false" enables path reads
/file stops consulting the opt-in at all (the ban's primary category returns)
/file goes back to isfile-then-extension, restoring the existence oracle
the realpath containment answer is inverted to always-contained (the gate goes inert)
the realpath gate compares against the LEXICAL base, so a symlinked subfolder stops being writable
the file resolver drops the realpath gate (a symlink out of the sandbox becomes deletable)
the batch mutation cap is dropped (one request can hand the server an unbounded delete list)
the counting walk loses its early exit, so a huge tree is walked in full before the cap can refuse
mutations.before:
if limit is not None and n_files + n_dirs > limit:
            break

mutations.label: the rmdir ceiling is dropped (recursive rmtree is unbounded again)
the too-large refusal answers 409 with counts, which the frontend reads as confirm-and-retry -> loop
rmdir counts without the cap, so the ceiling is decided after a full walk
